meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did I find out about my son's zero from his phone, Hale?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in from somewhere else. I'm writing those times down. Where is the rest of your evidence?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What does your procedure say about that?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Kids misquote things all the time, Hale. A wrong line is a wrong line, so what makes it more than that?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. It isn't close. I'll want all of this in an email tonight, so what are you actually proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising, Hale. What do you say to that?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. To put this behind him, he'll do the rewrite, private, before December 1, with nothing on his record. I want that in writing tonight, and my other questions will be in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm it with Owen. Put the day, the time and the room in the email tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen after school on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want my questions answered on who decided the zero and whether Owen was spoken to before it was entered. I expect your confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite before December 1 with nothing on his record, and she still wants answers on who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard first. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times, which moved her because it was dated, specific and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero early, answered each of her defences with something checkable, and put 4.4 on the table at the right moment.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence of late-night edits on October 28, the night before the essay was due, came close to that night, which is why she wrote the times down. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided the zero and whether Owen was spoken to first, answer both questions directly before moving to your documents.
